_comment: Pinned values for `dev-guardian ci-init` (Task 21). One data file so a release can refresh every SHA/checksum here in one place, instead of hunting them through three per-host YAML templates. Every action is pinned by FULL commit SHA (never a floating major-version tag like `@v7`); every scanner binary is pinned by version and a sha256 verified against the tool's own GitHub release (downloaded and independently hashed, not merely copied from the release's own checksums file). `version` fields are the human-readable comment dev-guardian appends after each pinned SHA. See README below each block for how each value was obtained and when.

actions._readme: Full commit SHA per action, verified via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/tags` (2026-09-25) — NOT `.../git/refs/tags/<tag>`, which resolves an ANNOTATED tag object rather than the commit it points at for some of these repos. `tags` already resolves to the commit SHA GitHub Actions itself checks out for `uses: owner/repo@<tag>`.

upload_sarif._note: github/codeql-action is a monorepo; upload-sarif is one action inside it, versioned with the whole repo's own release tags.

setup_dotnet._note: GitHub-only: scan_sast's .NET analyzers need the SDK, which gitlab/bitbucket document as a requirement instead of installing (see each template's own header comment).

attest_build_provenance._note: `ci-init github --attest` only. Resolved 2026-09-28 with `gh api repos/actions/attest-build-provenance/tags` and cross-checked with `git ls-remote` (a lightweight tag: both name the same commit). Since v4 it is a composite wrapper around actions/attest, itself pinned by SHA inside it (508db95d…, v4.2.1).

upload_artifact._note: `ci-init github --attest` only: the scan job keeps the two reports for the attest job, and so anyone verifying can download what was attested. Resolved the same way, same day.

download_artifact._note: `ci-init github --attest` only: the attest job fetches the reports the scan job kept. Resolved the same way, same day.

scanners._readme: Linux amd64 binaries only — every generated pipeline template runs on a Linux CI image (ubuntu-latest / a Debian-based container). Each url/sha256 pair was downloaded and hashed independently with `sha256sum` (2026-09-25), then cross-checked against the release's own published checksums file; both agreed for all three. `archive_member` is the exact path this task found the binary at inside that same downloaded tarball (`tar -tzf`, 2026-09-25) — all three ship it bare at the archive root, not nested under a `<name>_<version>_<os>_<arch>/` directory the way some projects do; re-run `tar -tzf` against the new tarball and update this field (never assume it is unchanged) whenever a version bump changes `linux_amd64_url`. bandit/semgrep/zizmor are pip-distributed (pipx) rather than a single release binary, so they are pinned by exact version instead of a hand-fetched sha256 — pip DOES verify each downloaded wheel's hash against what PyPI's own index recorded for that exact version (real integrity: catches a corrupted or tampered-in-transit download), but that is a WEAKER guarantee than `--require-hashes` against a pinned constraints file, which also catches the index itself later serving something different under the same name+version; `--require-hashes` needs a full transitive dependency hash list and is out of scope for a two-line pipx install of an exact version.

trivy._note: Same tag as TRIVY_INSTALL_TAG in mcp/src/runners/installCatalog.ts — keep both in step when either is bumped; test/unit/configs/pinnedCiData.test.ts asserts they agree.

bandit._note: pipx install bandit[toml]==<version> — verified current on PyPI 2026-09-25; same version and [toml] extra as installCatalog.ts's own bandit entry (needed if the scanned project has a pyproject.toml `[tool.bandit]` section).

semgrep._note: pipx install semgrep==<version> — verified current on PyPI 2026-09-25.

zizmor._note: pipx install zizmor==<version> — verified current on PyPI 2026-09-25.
